results.locator: PDF pp. 1–5, Abstract and Results including Fig. 4; source PDF 14 pp

fire-2026-nature.version: Exact publisher PDF retrieved and SHA-256 checked on 6 November 2026; 3 November 2026
fire-2026-nature.publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed scenario projection; no adaptation assumed

access.scope: Targeted source-and-analysis examination of the cited passages from the full downloaded PDF; not a full replication, all-appendix inspection or blanket whole-paper audit.

results.support: Spatial risk is the projected expected number of structures damaged or destroyed, conditional on burned area, structure exposure and vulnerability. Relative to 2011–2020, the three climate-model risk multipliers are 1.85, 2.27, and 3.2 in 2051–2060.

limits.locator: PDF pp. 9–13; Discussion, Methods and sensitivity analysis

model.locator: PDF pp. 2–4, 11–13, 20–22; Introduction, dynamic model, calibration and recovery of discount factors
model.support: Remote sensing and economic data identify gross extraction, recharge, marginal extraction costs and production; model-derived decision discount factors are compared with Ramsey and market benchmarks, with some aquifers omitted if the model cannot rationalize observed use.

effects.locator: Manuscript pp. 2–4 and 18–22; aggregate impulse responses and transmission
effects.support: A shock normalized to raise energy prices by 1% lowers emissions about 0.75% at peak, GDP and consumption about 0.3%, with indirect income and employment channels accounting for roughly two-thirds of consumption response.

distribution.locator: Manuscript pp. 3–4 and household-incidence section; UK expenditure and income responses; pp. 21–22 approximate cost calculation
